question.text: If <math><mi>α</mi></math> is the only real root of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo><</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> then the value of <math><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math> is (where, <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></mfenced></math> represents the greatest integer function)

solution.text:
Let, fx=x3+bx2+cx+1
fx=0 has only one real root so it is an increasing function
Now, f0=1,f-1=-1+b-c+1
f-1=b-c<0
using mean value theorem, real root must lie between -1,0
so, α=-1
α=1
